clue.text: Mat over hollow surface is wrinkled

parts.note: a mat is a rug
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: a hollow word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A doormat laid on an uneven floor has gone all creased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties 'surface' to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose is a botanical and zoological term for a ridged, corrugated surface.

clue.text: Captains fish in empty seas

indicators.note: the fish sits in the middle of the emptied seas
emptying a word removes its inside letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Ship's masters go fishing on barren oceans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' and 'in' look like the surface's barren seas, but they are the signals: the ends of the seas are kept and the fish goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a small ship or the captain of a team.

clue.text: Strange numbers raised price in betting shop

parts.note: odd means strange

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Peculiar figures have gone up on the bookmaker's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NOS upward into SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on is a betting price where the stake exceeds the possible winnings, for a favourite.

clue.text: Demonstrate in favour of group returning to Thailand

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: a returning word comes back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a set is a group
T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A supporters' group heads back to Thailand to stage a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to object publicly, which is what demonstrators do.

clue.text: Master forced to group pupils by ability

indicators.note: the letters are forced out of their order into a new one

explanation.surface: A headmaster is compelled to sort his classes by talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: to stream is to put school pupils into ability bands.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaming is the British school practice of setting classes by attainment level.

clue.text: Case of sunstroke initially stopping nice tan developing

indicators.note: the letter stops up a gap inside the rearranged letters
a tan developing changes shape, so the letters are rearranged
initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone acquiring a lovely tan suffers a bout of sunstroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges NICE TAN to INTANCE, and 'stopping' plugs S (from 'sunstroke initially') into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example or occurrence, as in 'a case in point'.

clue.text: Attractive (male) doctor keeping old lady's back in good condition

parts.note: hunky describes a ruggedly attractive man

indicators.note: the doctor keeps the old letter held inside
a word's back is its final letter

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain lady, whose back is wanted

explanation.surface: A handsome doctor looking after an old woman's spine keeps her in fine shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts O inside DR, giving DOR; 'back' then adds Y, the last letter of 'lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine, satisfactory, everything going well.

clue.text: Nasty smell from yeast in kitchen

indicators.note: the answer is drawn from within the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Fermenting yeast in the kitchen gives off an unpleasant odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink is a strong offensive odour.

clue.text: Mixture of material made up of different substances used where builders work

parts.words: material made up of different substances
parts.note: compo is a composition material such as mortar mixed from sand, cement and lime
builders work on a building site

explanation.surface: Builders on site use a blended material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a link word; COMPO is the trade name for mixed mortar or plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A composite is a thing made of several parts or ingredients combined, a blend.

clue.text: Pounds of British food

parts.note: eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Sounds like a question about the price of British grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money, but it is the verb: hits repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound something is to strike it repeatedly, to beat it.

clue.text: Animal with large hood

parts.note: a cow is an animal
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A beast wearing a big hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a monk's hood or hooded cloak.

clue.text: Son never swimming in river

indicators.note: swimming letters move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy who never takes a dip in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges NEVER to EVERN. The SEVERN is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a river, the longest in Great Britain.

clue.text: Disturbance about Turkish leader in European parliament

parts.note: a storm is a disturbance or uproar
on means about, concerning

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: An uproar over a Turkish politician breaks out in a European assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: STORMONT is the seat of the Northern Ireland Assembly in Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont houses Northern Ireland's devolved legislature, a parliament in Europe.

clue.text: Couple suffering most woe

indicators.note: the letters suffer, being knocked out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair of people who are enduring the greatest sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people together, a couple.

clue.text: Big women going up and down on one leg

parts.words: going up and down on one leg
parts.note: hopping is jumping on one leg

explanation.surface: Large women are bouncing about on one foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Whopping is informal for huge, very large.

clue.text: People adopting independent manner

indicators.note: the people take the letter in, holding it inside them

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: People take on a self-reliant bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing, their demeanour.

clue.text: Tradesman taking plane initially to timber

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: lumber is timber sawn into planks

explanation.surface: A craftsman uses a plane on wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests a carpenter's tool, but only its first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a tradesman who fits and repairs water pipes.

clue.text: Fish stew consumed in grotty motel

indicators.note: the eaten word goes in amongst the other letters
grotty means shabby and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone ate a fish stew at a seedy motel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotty' is the anagram signal, not a review of the motel; 'in' is the containment signal, with the meal eaten going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelote is a French dish of fish cooked in a wine and onion sauce.

clue.text: Put together dish containing a bit of lemon to follow starters of chilled Ogen melon

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first in the answer
the starters of words are their first letters
the dish holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a pie is a dish

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone assembles a meal where a pie with lemon comes after a chilled melon starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' is a menu joke: it means first letters. Ogen is a small sweet melon variety. 'containing' and 'to follow' set the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to assemble or gather things into a collection.

clue.text: Doctor wearing redder old hat

indicators.note: the word that wears the doctor has it inside, like clothing round a body

parts.note: sorer means more inflamed, hence redder
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor in a redder old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redder' is read as more inflamed or painful, as a sore spot is red; 'wearing' puts the doctor inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Support in reverse

explanation.surface: Help given while going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup supports; backing up a car means moving it rearwards.

clue.text: Mostly stupid new Sunday exercises

indicators.note: made new, the letters are arranged afresh
mostly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Silly new workouts done on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts 'stupid' to STUPI, and 'new' rearranges that to SITUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are stomach exercises raising the body from lying to sitting.

clue.text: Travel guide translated phrase

indicators.note: translated letters are converted into another form, a new order

explanation.surface: A phrasebook's expression has been put into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travel guide' suggests a book, but it is a Himalayan mountain guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sherpa is a Himalayan people famed as mountain porters and guides.

clue.text: Spot, say, for fish

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken and sounds like the answer

parts.note: a spot is a place

explanation.surface: Pick out a good place to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish.

clue.text: Place for special card

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A slot set aside for a particular card.
explanation.definitionFit: A space is a room or area, a place set aside.

clue.text: Increase penalty in the end following misery initially at a Shetland winter festival

indicators.note: the letter comes after the misery in the answer

parts.note: up means to increase
hell is misery

indicators.note: in the end points to the word's last letter
initially points to the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A harsh punishment ends in suffering at a Shetland festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places the end of 'penalty' after the misery; 'initially' applies to 'at'. Up Helly Aa is a Viking fire festival held in Lerwick, Shetland, each January.
explanation.definitionFit: Up Helly Aa is a midwinter fire festival in the Shetland Islands.

clue.text: Tin with old-fashioned tobacco

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
out means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Pipe tobacco in an antique tin.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOUT is British prison slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is slang, especially in prisons, for tobacco or cigarettes.

clue.text: Soprano interrupting tap dancing in polished comedy

indicators.note: the combined letters go inside the polished word

parts.note: slick means polished and smooth

indicators.note: the singer breaks into the middle of the rearranged letters
dancing letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer cuts into a tap routine in a smooth comedy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges the tap into APT, 'interrupting' breaks it with the soprano to make APST, and 'in' sets that inside the polished word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy of pratfalls and custard pies.
